name: Hospitalfield
funding: £839k income (FY2025); Creative Scotland, Historic Environment Scotland, National Lottery Heritage Fund, Foyle Foundation, Robertson Trust, Garfield Weston Foundation, William Grant Foundation.

name: The Bowes Museum
funding: £3.9M income (FY2025). Arts Council England, Durham County Council, National Lottery Heritage Fund £250k, Wolfson Foundation, Swire Charitable Trust, Art Fund, about 20 other trusts; Darlington Building Society, Global Radio.

name: Holburne Museum
funding: Public funders are the National Lottery Heritage Fund and Community Fund. Trusts include Garfield Weston, AKO, Clore Duffield and the Blavatnik Family Foundation; Bloomberg Philanthropies backed the website.

name: Belfast Exposed
funding: Arts Council of Northern Ireland and Belfast City Council, per its support page. A 2024 interview adds trusts and foundations, unnamed.

name: Golden Thread Gallery
funding: £400k income (FY2025); Arts Council NI, National Lottery, Belfast City Council, Art Fund, Gulbenkian, Ireland Funds, Ampersand, Future Screens NI.

name: The MAC
funding: £3.0M income (FY2025). Arts Council NI £1.1M, Belfast City Council £120k, Freelands Foundation £126k, Art Fund, Henry Moore Foundation, Dormant Accounts; sponsors include Clever Fulton Rankin.

name: De La Warr Pavilion
funding: £3.9M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £518k and Rother District Council £477k core; Esmée Fairbairn, Art Fund, Levelling Up Fund, National Lottery Heritage Fund.

name: Eastside Projects
funding: Arts Council England National Portfolio, Birmingham City University (partner since 2008), and trusts including the Paul Hamlyn, Esmée Fairbairn, Jerwood and Henry Moore foundations.

name: Ikon Gallery
funding: Arts Council England supports it with National Lottery funding. Current corporate patrons: Deutsche Bank, Elonex, Howells, Kier and Transport for West Midlands.

name: Wysing Arts Centre
funding: £863k income (FY2025); ACE NPO, Freelands Fdn (Murdoch media money), Garfield Weston, Ragdoll, Art Fund, local councils, Thalia Waste.

name: Arnolfini
funding: Arts Council England, Bristol City Council and UWE Bristol, which owns Bush House and leases the gallery space back. Ashley Clinton and Barker-Mill Trust is also credited.

name: Kettle's Yard
funding: University of Cambridge gallery. Arts Council England, Research England, Cambridge City Council; corporate supporters include David Zwirner, Emmanuel College, Murray Edwards College, City Asset and Resolute AV.
